npu.name: Qwen3 8B (INT4-CW)
npu.notes: Recommended (proven). Best quality verified for NPU.

npu.name: SmolLM3 3B (INT4-CW)
npu.notes: Tested on 285K NPU: 23.3 tok/s. New in OpenVINO 2026.3; also runs GPU/CPU.

npu.name: SmolLM3 3B (INT8-CW)
npu.notes: Tested on 285K NPU: 12.3 tok/s. Half the speed of INT4-CW, better quality headroom.

npu.name: LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct (INT4-CW)
npu.notes: Tested on 285K NPU (NPU 3, Arrow Lake): 38.8 tok/s — fastest verified NPU model. NPU-only build (fails CPU/GPU, see model card). WARNING: on Lunar Lake (Core Ultra 200V, NPU 4) it produces word salad at full speed — NPU drivers 32.0.100.4778 and .5540, OpenVINO 2026.3.0/2026.3.1/2026.5-nightly all alike, Intel's own LFM2.5 exports too — a driver update does not fix it (verified 2026-09-01; see TODONT). Arrow Lake / Meteor Lake NPUs only until that is fixed.

npu.name: Phi 3.5 Mini (INT4-CW)
npu.notes: Proven. Smaller and faster than Qwen3 8B, lower quality.

npu.name: DeepSeek R1 Distill 1.5B (INT4-CW)
npu.notes: Tested: works but terrible quality. Smoke-test/dev use only.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3.8 27B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Needs OpenVINO 2026.3.1+ (the 2026.3.1 release enabled it; install.ps1 pulls it). Pinned to the repo's 2026.3.1 branch on purpose: its main branch is a 2026.4-toolchain export that SEGFAULTS the 2026.3.x runtime at load. Verified 2026-08-30 on Arc 140V (2026.3.1 release): correct answers, 3.6-4.8 tok/s — dense 27B, so the 15 GB must be resident (24 GB card, or a raised iGPU shared-memory budget) and --offload-ratio does nothing. Quality over speed; a 24-core CPU is ~2-3 tok/s. Template pre-seeds <think>; NoLlama detects that at load.

gpu_vlm.name: Muse Glimmer 30B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Intel's official export (2026-08-12), enabled in the OpenVINO 2026.3.1 release. Lands on a VLM slot with tool calling + prefix caching. Verified 2026-08-30 on Arc 140V (2026.3.1): quotes the instruction back verbatim, answers correctly, ~2.5 tok/s (17 GB on a shared-memory iGPU); ~14 tok/s on an Arc Pro B60. The Xe2/Xe3 GPU corruption seen 2026-08 was the optimum path only — this GenAI path was never affected. Always reasons by default; the web UI's 'Just answer me' trims it.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3-VL 8B (INT8)
gpu_vlm.notes: Verified 2026-06-16 on Arc 140V in dual mode (NPU text + GPU vision): correct color/shape ID, ~6s. INT8 retains OCR/number detail better than INT4 at ~9 GB; fits a 16 GB ARC. One generation behind Qwen3.5, but the most thoroughly verified GPU vision pairing for Qwen3-8B on NPU.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: The power pick IF your GPU has XMX (Arc/Lunar Lake — install.ps1 says so above): multimodal MoE, 26.6 tok/s on Arc 140V, 21.0 on a 24-core CPU, 262k context. Best of the three Gemma 4 exports and prefix caching works (re-verified 2026-08-21 on Arc Pro B60, loads in ~40s). It also runs on a non-XMX iGPU when the memory is there: 8.4 tok/s vision / 11.1 text on an Arc 140T with a 64 GB shared budget (community, issue #24, 2026-08-31) — XMX gates disk offload, not loading. CAVEAT: its KV is 240 KB/token, so the auto-sized pool lands on its 2 GB floor — about 8k tokens. Pin --cache-size-gb before pointing an agent at it; NoLlama warns at load.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 E4B (INT8)
gpu_vlm.notes: Runs on every device class except NPU: 16.4 tok/s on Arc 140V, ~13 on CPU. Reads fine detail its E2B sibling cannot. This is OUR re-export (2026-08-21) — Intel's OpenVINO/gemma-4-E4B-it-int8-ov traced attention decomposed, so it can get NO prefix caching at all; ours has the fused SDPA op, so caching works (~2.6x faster per turn on a repeated agent prompt) with byte-identical answers. Reported upstream. Intel's build is ~2.2x faster on a cold turn, so prefer theirs for one-shot vision.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3.5 4B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Newest Qwen VLM generation (Qwen2.5-VL -> Qwen3-VL -> Qwen3.5). Verified on Arc 140V 2026-08-07: 27 tok/s VLM streaming. Reads text in images well but confidently invents product identities from logos — prompt for visible features only.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3-VL 8B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Recommended. One generation behind Qwen3.5. Verified on Xe-LPG iGPU for OCR, color/count, no hallucination on empty input. Like all VLMs, prone to confident hallucination on ambiguous images (e.g., invented make/model/year from unbadged photos) — prompt for visible features only and ask for uncertainty explicitly.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen2.5-VL 3B (INT8)
gpu_vlm.notes: Recommended (proven). INT8 retains fine detail (OCR, numbers) better than INT4. Research license (non-commercial) — see model card.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 E2B Vision (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Tested 2026-08-21 on Arc Pro B60 (2026.3): loads, prefix caching works, reads large text and colours/shapes correctly. Weakest of the Gemma 4 exports — misreads small glyphs and then claims "the image is missing" rather than saying it cannot resolve them, which is a model quirk, not a broken image path. Efficient (E2B = effective-2B) successor to Gemma 3. Needs OpenVINO 2026.2+. Measured on Arc 140T: 14.5 tok/s vision / 18.8 text — quickest on text of the small VLMs tested there, though Qwen3-VL-4B int4 is faster on images (community, issue #24, 2026-08-31).

whisper.name: Whisper Base (INT8)
whisper.notes: Fastest. Multi-language. Pre-exported — no conversion step (just a small, quick download).

whisper.name: Whisper Small (INT8)
whisper.notes: Good balance. Multi-language. Pre-exported — no conversion step (small, quick download).

whisper.name: Whisper Medium (INT8)
whisper.notes: Best accuracy under 16 GB. Multi-language. Pre-exported — no conversion step (download still needed).

gpu_llm.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 14B (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Recommended for VS Code Copilot Chat / tool calling (--vscode-compat). Fits 16GB with KV headroom. Emits Hermes-style <tool_call> JSON, handled by parse_tool_calls. Newer Qwen3-Coder exists only as 30B-A3B (17GB, falls back to CPU on 16GB), so this is the best coder that fits.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Lighter Copilot/tool-calling option. Faster than the 14B, weaker on multi-step agent loops. Same Hermes tool-call format.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3 30B-A3B MoE (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Best quality. Needs >32 GB RAM (shared with system). Verified 2026-08-09 on 285K CPU via CB backend (smoke test). 262k context — holds a whole novel with --cache-size-gb 12.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3 Thinking 30B-A3B MoE (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Always-thinking sibling of the Instruct 30B-A3B, same int4 recipe (our export — no Intel pre-export exists). Verified 2026-08-09 on 285K CPU: multi-step reasoning then a correct answer. Output ends thinking with </think> (no opening tag); give it max_tokens headroom or the reasoning eats the budget.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3 Coder 30B-A3B MoE (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Code-focused MoE. Needs >32 GB RAM (shared with system).
